pages.title: Your Citizens
pages.text: The Charter assigns citizens to each colony as the Town Hall is upgraded. A citizen is not, strictly, the Foreman's $(o)employee$() — they are the Charter's worker, on loan, audited at the same cycle as the rest of the books.$(br2)A senior Foreman keeps them fed, housed, and in honest work. The Charter rewards this in tax credit at audit.

pages.title: Trades the Charter Recognises
pages.text: $(l)Builder$() — Erik's trade. The first hire on every colony.$(br2)$(l)Forester$() — wood at scale.$(br2)$(l)Miner$() — stone, ore, the deep terraces.$(br2)$(l)Farmer / Fisher$() — food, without which the audit fails.$(br2)$(l)Smelter$() — ingots at scale.$(br2)$(l)Guard$() — the Charter does not provide armies, but it provides Guards.$(br2)$(l)Mechanic$() — Workshop-tier. Comes in late. Worth the wait.

A citizen who falls in service is, on the Charter's audit, $(o)"transferred to permanent rest, with thanks."$() The Charter pays the Foreman a small docket-credit and seeds a replacement at the next survey.$(br2)Most senior Foremen learn their citizens' names anyway.
